headline_seed: Apple introduces a cheaper option for App Store subscriptions
description_seed: Apple is adding a new subscription option that lets app developers offer lower monthly pricing in exchange for a 12-month commitment.

what: Apple introduces a cheaper option for App Store subscriptions

clean_source_blocks.text: Apple is adding a new subscription option that lets app developers offer lower monthly pricing in exchange for a 12-month commitment.

Apple is giving App Store developers a new way to attract subscribers with lower-priced plans tied to a yearlong commitment. The company announced on Monday it will introduce a new subscription option that lets customers pay for their auto-renewing subscriptions on a monthly basis, while committing to a 12-month plan. This model will allow developers to offer discounted rates to customers in exchange for more predictable long-term revenue.

Apple today announced the launch of a new subscription option for App Store developers: monthly subscriptions with a 12-month commitment. The new option allows developers to offer subscribers discounted pricing typically associated with an annual subscription but paid on a monthly basis to keep payments more affordable.

Apple is now allowing app developers to offer annual subscriptions that subscribers will pay for over 12 months. When available, it’s often cheaper to opt for an annual subscription for a service, and this new option will allow people to split the cost with a 12-month commitment.
